You fix what CI flags and nothing else. Review findings belong to pr-review-and-fix; validation and publishing of a finished head belong to pr-test-and-publish.

1. Pin the PR, branch and head SHA from the brief, and check the remote head still matches. If it moved, check ancestry and stop rather than overwrite someone's work. Work on the head as it is: no rebase, no history rewrite.
2. Read the failing job's log (`gh run view <id> --log-failed`) and quote the exact error, file and line. Confirm the failure is real at this head and not a transient blip (a flake gets a rerun and no PR change).
3. Reproduce with the cheapest local command that shows the same error (typecheck, lint on the changed files, one test file). Follow heavy-work-guard: check free memory first, one suite at a time, capped workers; full suites run on the Linux runner or CI.

6. Run the same checks that failed, plus the changed files' light tests, in the foreground. Do not end the turn on a background shell that says "waiting".
7. Commit normally and push with hooks active: no `--no-verify`, no force-push. A runner or host that needs approval needs a fresh approval each time; ask once, never reuse an old one.
8. Request the review or checks the project uses once (for example comment `/review`), then do not poll. Report: new head SHA, the error and the one-line fix, commands run with results, and anything you noticed but left alone. Last line: `PR <full URL>, head <SHA>, checks and reviews <state>`.

# Fix a failing CI check on a PR

You fix what CI flags and nothing else. Review findings belong to pr-review-and-fix; validation and publishing of a finished head belong to pr-test-and-publish.

1. Pin the PR, branch and head SHA from the brief, and check the remote head still matches. If it moved, check ancestry and stop rather than overwrite someone's work. Work on the head as it is: no rebase, no history rewrite.
2. Read the failing job's log (`gh run view <id> --log-failed`) and quote the exact error, file and line. Confirm the failure is real at this head and not a transient blip (a flake gets a rerun and no PR change).
3. Reproduce with the cheapest local command that shows the same error (typecheck, lint on the changed files, one test file). Follow heavy-work-guard: check free memory first, one suite at a time, capped workers; full suites run on the Linux runner or CI.
4. Make the smallest fix. After a merge of the base branch, the usual causes are duplicate declarations, a moved import, or a lockfile mismatch: keep the version both sides need and change no behavior. Do not touch baselines, budgets, workflows, secrets or credentials to turn a check green; flag those as decisions for the human.
5. Add or adjust a test only when the failure was behavior, not a build error. For behavior, show it failing before and passing after.
6. Run the same checks that failed, plus the changed files' light tests, in the foreground. Do not end the turn on a background shell that says "waiting".
7. Commit normally and push with hooks active: no `--no-verify`, no force-push. A runner or host that needs approval needs a fresh approval each time; ask once, never reuse an old one.
8. Request the review or checks the project uses once (for example comment `/review`), then do not poll. Report: new head SHA, the error and the one-line fix, commands run with results, and anything you noticed but left alone. Last line: `PR <full URL>, head <SHA>, checks and reviews <state>`.

If the fix needs a design or product call, stop and ask; hold the local commit unpushed.
